title: Ukulele, kazoo and starting on piano
summary: He started on ukulele and kazoo, took up piano when a neighborhood kid showed him up, heard Clarence Profit and Bobby Henderson at the YMCA, and did unpaid studio jobs with guitarist Jack Snead.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: When did you start playing...? Oh, you started playing the piano...
Yeah, on the piano... Well, first I played the ukelele.
I was pretty good on the ukelele. We used to do that. Then when I moved uptown... I have a picture of me when I was there. You should see it. I mean, he brought a couple of pictures.

Well, I started playing... I didn't play piano... I didn't get a chance to follow my interest in piano until a kid came on the block playing a little better than I do. I used to play the kazoo, and sometimes I used to play in
little groups, you know. So after that, this guy started to do everything on...taking me all over... Getting my face rubbed and all that! I said, "Oh well" -- I started playing the piano!
So, I remember when I started playing it sounded pretty good, and the rest of the time I... Before I went uptown, I heard Clarence Profit and Bobby Henderson play. That's the next...

In the YMCA. It was Splicky's(?)... And I played with Jack Snead, a guitar player...he played guitar, man... He was always a cook; he sold hot pies, patties and everything. He used to get me... We used to go... I remember I'd go down to all these studios, and we'd play, you know, in these studios! I never got paid; I got five dollars or something. He took me around, yeah...
